title: Terraform module contracts, testing, and stage-promotion for Private Control Plane
content:
Purpose and scope

This is a working doc for establishing a lightweight but repeatable pattern for Terraform module contracts, automated testing, and stage -> prod promotion specifically for the Private Control Plane (VPC / on-prem) components. The goal is to reduce hand edits during customer rollouts, make upgrades safer, and let module authors and operators agree on stable interfaces.

This doc focuses on: module interface contracts, CI testing harnesses (unit, integration), remote state and locking conventions, staging promotion workflow (dev -> stage -> prod), and pre/post-upgrade checks. It intentionally does NOT dive into low-level Kubernetes manifests or the application-level migration steps — those are other runbooks.

Assumptions 
- We manage Terraform modules in mono-repo infra-private-controlplane/modules.
- Remote state is S3-compatible with DynamoDB locking for AWS-hosted installs; equivalent object store + lock service for customer on-prem mirrors same pattern.
- Each customer deployment uses a dedicated state per environment (dev, stg, prod) and a central registry of module versions.
- CI has access to ephemeral creds for integration testing in a sandbox account/cluster.

Problem statements this doc addresses
- Operators get surprised by module input changes (breaking or implicit behavior).
- Rollouts currently rely on manual checklist and ad-hoc smoke tests.
- Lack of automated promotion between stage/prod for module releases.
- No consistent testing harness for module authors to validate behavior before tagging.

High-level pattern (one-liner)
- Define explicit module contract (inputs/outputs + semantic stability policy), require automated tests (plan assertions + integration apply in sandbox), publish signed release artifacts, and promote with a controlled pipeline that executes pre- and post-checks on customer-like staging before allowing production update.

Module contract conventions (required)
- Each module MUST include a file CONTRACT.md at module root with: purpose, public inputs (stable), private inputs (experimental), outputs consumers may rely on, and upgrade policy.
- Inputs that are considered stable must be flagged with a versioned semantic comment: // stable-v1.0.
- Outputs intended for external consumption must be prefixed with "export_" (e.g., export_control_plane_endpoint). This reduces accidental coupling on internal outputs.
- Avoid using dynamic keys as outputs (no map-by-generated-id) unless contract documents the key shape.
- Modules MUST be backward-compatible within a minor version (x.y+). Breaking changes force major version bump and an upgrade note.

Module structure example (convention)
- modules/controlplane-gateway/
  - main.tf
  - variables.tf
  - outputs.tf
  - CONTRACT.md
  - examples/
  - test/ (see testing below)

Remote state and locking
- State naming: <customer>-<env>-private-cp.tfstate (example: acme-stg-private-cp.tfstate)
- S3 bucket: inf-state-<region>-redwood (encrypted SSE-KMS), with lifecycle + versioning enabled.
- State encryption: SSE-KMS with a customer-managed CMK for private deployments where required.
- Locking: DynamoDB table named tfstate-locks.<region> with 10RCU write capacity (autoscale) — adjust per tenant scale.
- State protection policy: no direct console edits except documented emergency procedures. Always prefer 'terraform apply' or 'state mv' via reviewed PRs.

Testing harness (local + CI)
Requirements: fast feedback for authors (unit plan tests) + integration apply in sandbox for every module change that touches resources.

1) Unit / plan-time tests (fast)
- Implement a harness that runs terraform init + terraform plan with deterministic inputs and asserts plan contains expected resource counts and that no unexpected destroy occurs.
- Use terratest or a lightweight shell wrapper that checks for specific resource addresses in the plan JSON.
- Example assertions: module should not create IAM Role{,Policy} by default unless enabled; module must output export_control_plane_endpoint; changing a stable input should produce only expected replacements.

2) Integration (apply) tests in sandbox (slower)
- Run a full apply against a disposable sandbox environment (shared sandbox account or kube cluster).
- Validate: resources reach ready state, perform a smoke API call through gateway, verify KV cache persists across restart for stateful components where relevant.
- Teardown: destroy resources, but keep logs/artifacts for debugging failed runs.

3) Safety guards in CI
- Require successful plan tests + integration apply for PR merges that change module code.
- PRs that change CONTRACT.md or variables marked as stable must include a short upgrade note in the PR body with migration steps.

Semantic versioning, publishing, and module registry
- Module authors must tag releases using SemVer. Minor releases (x.y) should not include breaking changes.
- Build pipeline will create a release artifact with: module code tarball, CONTRACT.md snapshot, plan-test matrix results, integration-test log URLs. Publish to internal module registry (git tags + artifacts bucket) and create a release entry in CONFLUENCE-CP-ARCH.
- Signed releases: CI will sign the artifact checksum using the build GPG key so operators can verify integrity before applying to critical environments.

Stage promotion flow (dev -> stg -> prod)
1) Dev (author sandbox): module author develops and iterates. All tests green locally/CI.
2) Staging promotion: create release tag and trigger 'promote-to-stg' pipeline. This pipeline will:
   - Apply module changes to a staging tenant that mirrors customer config (size, KMS, similar network topology).
   - Run canary smoke tests (see pre/post checks below).
   - Wait for manual approval gate (owner + release manager).
3) Production promotion: after gate, run 'promote-to-prod' pipeline which:
   - Creates a maintenance window ticket into JIRA-DEPLOY-1741 with estimated risk and rollback steps.
   - Applies to prod using batched, region-by-region rollouts if multi-region.
   - Runs post-apply health checks and synthetic transactions.

Pre-apply checks (must-run)
- terraform validate + fmt check.
- drift detection: run 'terraform plan' against current prod state from last-known commit and ensure diff is only intended changes.
- backup remote state snapshot (s3 copy + version) and create a backup ticket.
- verify module artifact checksum matches release checksum.
- verify KMS keys referenced exist and key policy allows current operator principal.

Post-apply checks (smoke + rollback detection)
- Verify control plane pods reach Ready and sufficient replicas.
- Run 5 minute synthetic test: issue 100 requests at target QPS to gateway and check 99% requests succeed and latency p50/p95 within baseline.
- If <90% success or error rate spikes, trigger automated rollback path (see Rollback section).

Rollback policy and fast path
- Major failure definition: control plane unavailable for >2 minutes or persistent error >5% for 10 minutes.
- Fast rollback: revert to last known good module version and apply with state snapshot restore if needed.
- Slow rollback: if state migration is irreversible, follow the migration-rollback runbook (separate doc). Always notify customer success and SRE channel.

Upgrade / rotations (KMS, certs, etc.)
- KMS rotation: create a new key, update module variable to point to key_arn_new, promote to staging and validate decrypt/encrypt surface. Do not retire old key until all secrets re-encrypted and a 72-hour stability window observed.
- TLS cert rotation: use gradual rotation using extra SAN and rolling update across gateway replicas. Test with synthetic clients that validate cert chain.
- Secrets rotation: for on-prem, ensure secret store (Vault/SSM) credentials are rotated in both infra and application layers; include step to re-seal/unseal vault copies where needed.

Operational checklists (quick reference)
Before applying (operators):
- [ ] Confirm release tag and artifact checksum
- [ ] Snapshot remote state + upload copy to secure archive with timestamp
- [ ] Confirm scheduled maintenance window + notify stakeholders
- [ ] Ensure DynamoDB lock table active and capacity ok
- [ ] Run terraform plan and annotate PR with plan outputs

Immediately after apply:
- [ ] Wait until all control plane pods in Ready state
- [ ] Run synthetic 100-request smoke test, record metrics
- [ ] Inspect logs for new error spikes in last 10 minutes
- [ ] If metrics bad -> run rollback plan

Module author checklist (before merge)
- [ ] CONTRACT.md updated if public interface changed
- [ ] Unit plan assertions added for new behavior
- [ ] Integration test added/updated and green on CI sandbox
- [ ] Upgrade notes included in PR body for operators

Open questions / TODOs
- Define a minimal plan-assertions DSL (json/yaml) to standardize plan checks across modules. Right now different modules use different scripts; maintenance burden.
- Decide on one canonical sandbox environment per region vs per team. Currently runs are in a generic sandbox that diverges from prod in subtle network ways.
- Should we require signed release artifacts for all customer-facing updates or only for major/minor releases?
- Add a small "preview" capability for customers to opt-in into staged module upgrades before general rollout. Need product input.

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- View plan as JSON: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform show -json tfplan > tfplan.json
- Count resource addresses: jq '.resource_changes | length' tfplan.json
- Backup state: aws s3 cp s3://inf-state-us-west-2/redwood-prod.tfstate s3://inf-state-backups/redwood-prod.tfstate-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)
- Lock troubleshooting: aws dynamodb describe-table --table-name tfstate-locks.us-west-2

Notes to self: prioritize the plan-assertion DSL and a small library in Go/Python that runs uniformly in CI. Lia will own the sandbox consolidation experiment (cc @Lia).

End of draft.
